title: SurCo: Learning Linear SURrogates for COmbinatorial Nonlinear Optimization Problems
abstract: SurCo is a general-purpose method for solving combinatorial nonlinear optimization problems by learning linear surrogate costs that can be used in existing combinatorial solvers. SurCo has three variants: SurCo-zero for individual nonlinear problems, SurCo-prior for problem distributions, and SurCo-hybrid to combine both distribution and problem-specific information.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to optimize a complex system, like a logistics network or a financial portfolio. You want to find the best solution, but the problem is too hard to solve directly. SurCo's key idea is to learn a simpler, linear problem that approximates the original problem. This linear problem can be solved efficiently using existing solvers, and the solution can be used as a good approximation to the original problem.

Think of it like using a map to navigate a city. The map is a simplified representation of the city, but it's much easier to use than trying to navigate the actual city.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
SurCo works by learning a linear surrogate cost function that approximates the original nonlinear problem. This is done by optimizing a loss function that measures the difference between the original problem and the linear surrogate. The linear surrogate is then used to solve the problem, and the solution is refined using a fine-tuning process.

For example, in the embedding table sharding problem, SurCo learns a linear surrogate cost function that approximates the nonlinear latency function.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
SurCo has been evaluated on several benchmark problems, including embedding table sharding, photonic inverse design, and nonlinear route planning. The results show that SurCo outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of solution quality and runtime.

For example, in the embedding table sharding problem, SurCo achieves a 20% reduction in latency compared to the best baseline method.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
SurCo has the potential to impact a wide range of applications, from logistics and finance to energy and healthcare. By providing a general-purpose method for solving combinatorial nonlinear optimization problems, SurCo can help practitioners and researchers to tackle complex problems that were previously unsolvable.

For example, in the field of logistics, SurCo can be used to optimize routes for delivery trucks, reducing fuel consumption and lowering emissions.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
SurCo's key innovations include its ability to learn a linear surrogate cost function that approximates the original nonlinear problem, and its use of a fine-tuning process to refine the solution. These innovations enable SurCo to outperform state-of-the-art methods and to tackle complex problems that were previously unsolvable.

For example, in the field of photonic inverse design, SurCo can be used to optimize the design of optical devices, such as lenses and mirrors.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
SurCo is an open-source software package that can be used to solve a wide range of combinatorial nonlinear optimization problems. To get started, simply download the SurCo package and follow the instructions in the user manual.

For example, you can use SurCo to optimize the design of a logistics network, or to optimize the routing of delivery trucks.
